small_guidance:
- The inner loop recomputes the same conv output 16 times (once per pool offset). Restructure so each thread computes each conv output position exactly once, then accumulates POOL*POOL convs into the pooled bin. This alone is a ~16x reduction in FLOPs.
- Increase BLOCK_P to 256 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3 to better hide memory latency on the long IC*KH*KW=72 inner reduction.
- Cache weights per (pid_oc) once into registers (only 8*3*3=72 floats) outside any spatial loop to avoid redundant tl.load on w_ptr.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as: one program per (N, OC, pool-tile). For each pool output position, loop kh_idx,kw_idx in [0,POOL) and compute the conv output at (ph*POOL+kh_idx, pw*POOL+kw_idx) exactly once, summing into a pooled accumulator. This matches the reference asymptotic cost (no shortcut) but removes the current 16x overcomputation.
- Switch to an im2col-style GEMM tile per program: tile output spatial positions (BLOCK_M) against OC (BLOCK_N) with reduction over IC*KH*KW (BLOCK_K=72 fits in one step). Fuse the pool reduction (divide by POOL*POOL after summing POOL*POOL output rows), sigmoid, and sum-over-(C,H,W) into the epilogue with an atomic_add to out[n].
- Consider persistent kernel per (N): each program handles a chunk of OC and accumulates the per-image scalar in shared memory, doing a single atomic_add at the end to minimize atomic traffic (currently N*OC*ceil(PH*PW/BLOCK_P) atomics).
